title: Decide the local interactive host scope reduction and its cascade
description:
## Decision needed

`chatticus-9af381` Phase A0 returned **1650x** at ~25 ms RTT — row three of the threshold table agreed in advance: *"Local interactive host is not viable. Keep accelerated batch, which never needed any of this."*

That is not a marginal call. **This task is to accept the scope reduction and follow it through the design**, or to argue explicitly why not. It is a decision, not an experiment.

## The cascade nobody has drawn yet

The local interactive host was the **only remaining consumer of the tunnel**:

| Wanted the outbound tunnel for | Still needs it after A0? |
|---|---|
| Local host mounting EFS (`fbae4e` D1/D2) | **No** — host class not viable |
| Reverse VNC for a local Antharchy VM (`3c6df9`) | **No** — goes away with the local GUI host |
| Accelerated batch (`fbae4e` D8) | **Never did** — object I/O only, SQS + scoped S3 |

So if the scope reduction is accepted, the following stop being work:

- **D2 entirely** — the WireGuard peer, the stopped-when-idle EC2 endpoint, the ~$0.65/mo idle floor, key distribution and rotation.
- **`0b10d6`'s consequence** — the Fargate `NET_ADMIN` finding remains true and becomes irrelevant, because there is no tunnel endpoint to place.
- **`9af381` Phase A and Phase B** — these exist to prove an out-of-VPC mount for a host class that no longer exists. They are **moot, not parked**. They are currently open pending CDK EFS + tunnel, which points at work that should not happen.
- **The local-VM half of `3c6df9`** — the display initiative survives for EC2 Antharchy, and worker-dials-out remains the right transport there, but the "same tunnel serves both storage and display" argument loses its second consumer.

## What survives

- **EFS for AWS hosts** — untouched by A0, still the high-value simplification, but now carrying its own unmeasured assumption. See `chatticus-3d5357` (in-VPC measurement) before building it.
- **Accelerated batch** — untouched. Never needed EFS, a tunnel, or a display. Still the highest-value host class, still blocked as *implementation* on a manifold job kind, which is blocked on routines not being implemented (`766c51`).
- **`ea918a`** — the actimeo/concurrency contradiction still needs deciding, and it applies to AWS hosts at default `actimeo`, not only to the dead local host.
- **`3c6df9` for EC2** — display on EC2 Antharchy, worker-dials-out.

## Caveat to weigh before accepting

A0's WAN verdict is robust (32 s wall, ~1 RTT per file, and real agent workloads do mutate trees). But A0's **mechanism** claim — that `actimeo` does not help — is confounded: each timed iteration rewrites the tree via `git checkout`, and the server was nfs-ganesha in Docker carrying a ~13x LAN tax of its own. See `chatticus-3d5357`.

That confound does **not** rescue the local interactive host: 1650x has too much headroom, and the WAN RTT term alone (~24 s of the 32 s) is independent of caching. It does mean the in-VPC extrapolation is open.

## Also worth weighing

The local interactive host was already the least valuable slice — ~$30–60/mo, against accelerated batch's $100s–$1000s per run. A0 removed the cheapest-to-support version of the one thing that justified the tunnel. Deleting the tunnel workstream is a larger simplification than the host class was ever worth.

## Done when

Either:

- **Accepted** — `9af381` closed as moot (not parked), D2 marked superseded in `chatticus-fbae4e`, the tunnel removed from `chatticus-3c6df9`'s transport section, and the epic's status updated so nobody builds toward a dead host class; or
- **Rejected** — with a recorded reason the 1650x result should not be taken at face value, and what would change it.

comments.text:
## Accepted 2026-09-07

Scope reduction accepted by the roadmap owner. The local interactive host is not a host class we pursue. Cascade applied:

- `chatticus-fbae4e` **D2 superseded** — no WireGuard peer, no stopped-when-idle EC2 endpoint, no key rotation, no ~$0.65/mo idle floor. The `0b10d6` Fargate finding stays on the record as verified fact; it is simply no longer load-bearing.
- **D6 moot** — no tunnel, so no tunnel-health signal to fold into the heartbeat.
- **D5 refuted** — A0 measured the mitigations failing at WAN latency. The mechanism claim stays open in-VPC via `3d5357`.
- **D1 narrowed** — "every host class" now means every AWS host, and is still unmeasured for hot working trees.
- **"Shared tunnel with the display path" withdrawn** in both initiatives.
- `chatticus-3c6df9` — worker-dials-out **retained** for EC2 Antharchy; it never depended on the storage tunnel. Local VM row dropped from the host table.
- `chatticus-9af381` closed as moot.

What survives: EFS for AWS hosts (D1, gated on `3d5357`), accelerated batch (D8, untouched), `ea918a` (still needs a product decision, applies to AWS hosts), and display on EC2.
